newsitem.title: USA: CityBird adds U.S. cargo routes.
newsitem.headline: CityBird adds U.S. cargo routes.

text.p: CityBird and its cargo partner Swissair Schweizerische Luftverkehr AG are coming to the United States beginning with Miami and Orlando and are offering passengers their signature low fares, a CityBird executive said Friday.

"We signed an agreement about three weeks ago with Swissair. They buy all of our world-wide cargo capacity and that covers the new Miami, Orlando and Mexico City service," Trevor Sadler, director of operations, told Reuters.
The Belgian flagship carrier is offering inaugural one-way passenger fares of $99 and introductory fares as low as $149 from now until June 22 to Brussels, the airline announced Friday.
CityBird will begin non-stop full-service flights on Wednesdays and Sundays from Miami to Brussels on March 30.
"It is a two step arrangement," said Sadler. Swissair gets a certain amount of space guaranteed and then can get more depending on passenger load, he said.

Although he declined to talk about pricing, he said the yield to CityBird is attractive. "We would have a building curve to arrive at ourselves," he said, adding that this arrangement saves costs of selling the space.
Currently American Airlines and Delta Airlines serve Brussels from Miami.
CityBird flies McDonnel-Douglas MD-11 widebody aircraft, the announcement said.

CityBird will also start non-stop service from Brussels to Mexico City on March 27. It will begin four flights weekly from Newark on June 2. Los Angeles will get twice per week service June 3 and San Francisco weekly on June 7.
CityBird is a subsidiary of City Hotels, S.A., Brussels. The U.S. headquarters is in Bethesda, Maryland.
